title: Consonant-vowels
paragraphs: I was enjoying the pleasant caressing of breeze, sitting on the beach.
The darkness of night was slowly swallowing the dusk, when a friend said, “Oh! The lights are already on,” forcing me to wake up from the trance.
Sitting near Gandhiji’s statue, I turned towards the northern direction to look at Aṇṇā’s statue and my mind raced back in memory lane.

The electrical poles erected near Aṇṇā’s statue were spilling light over me. My poetic elegy on the All India Radio on the eve of Aṇṇā’s demise rushed back to my memory. Or rather, I am sorry; when did I forget it for me to remember it?

> We looked up to you as our shade of life, > but you went in search of solace in the land off the sea. > Is this fair? > Establishing your supremacy among the > pearls underneath sea, > You sleep peacefully on the beach! > > Your tongue had mothered > Many a speech sweet like nākaswaram’s strain; > Why is it tied up now? > You wished to possess a heart > which could weather any shock.

> But can my frail heart > bear your loss added! > > ...... > ...... > > I know, it is conspiracy of Nature, > Aṇṇā .... you! > > Till the time I join you in > the abode you repose in, > kindly lend me your mighty heart, Aṇṇā! > I swear to present it at your lotus feet > When I join you, Aṇṇā.
Beads of tears swept my cheeks even when I was reciting the verse. On observing my melancholy, my friends tried to divert my attention by broaching sundry stories. At last, they came to square one.

A friend noted, “Just observe the peach of a gift Tamil has presented us. Aṇṇā with ‘a’ as the first letter in his name was our leader. Now it is Kalaiñar Karunanidhi with ‘ka’ as the first letter in his name.”
I intervened, “Sir, I am just the consonant /k/. It becomes the consonant-vowel ‘ka’ only when it combines with the vowel /a/ that begins Aṇṇā’s name.”
> A consonant-vowel is said > With vowel following the consonant. > > (Eḻuttatikāram : Nūl Marapu, verse 18)
